OSKAR [SURNAME]
Senior Full-Stack / Frontend Engineer

[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [GITHUB / PORTFOLIO]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior full-stack engineer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications. Strongest in frontend development with React and TypeScript, with hands-on experience building Node.js services and working with PostgreSQL. Experienced in onboarding and identity-verification features, secure document workflows, and leading delivery on a customer-facing mobile app. Also served as acting team lead for four months in 2024.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, React Native, Angular
Backend: Node.js, NestJS, Express, GraphQL, Apollo Server
Databases and data: PostgreSQL, TypeORM, Prisma
Cloud and messaging: AWS ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS, Firebase Cloud Messaging
Other: Laravel, WordPress, Terraform (small edits), Python (basic), YAML

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Fullstack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB | 2021–Present
- Build onboarding features using React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS.
- Delivered a Swedish BankID identity-verification step supporting QR-code and same-device flows through a provider SDK. A/B tested with 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Implemented a secure ID-document upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV virus scanning in Lambda, SQS status updates and PostgreSQL.
- Contributed to an incremental migration of the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, moving route by route behind the same API gateway.
- Maintained a backend-for-frontend (BFF) using Apollo Server and GraphQL.
- Served as acting team lead for four months in 2024 during the team lead’s parental leave, including 1:1s and sprint planning.

Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB | 2018–2021
- Delivered web and mobile projects for agency clients using Angular, React, React Native, Laravel and WordPress.
- Tech lead and primary app developer for a ferry-ticket mobile application, working in a two-developer team. Built the React Native and TypeScript app for purchasing and showing tickets offline; the other developer handled the payment backend. The app reached approximately 50,000 downloads.

Developer | Nordkust Media | 2014–2018
- Worked on newspaper websites.

SELECTED PROJECTS

Express to NestJS Migration | Älvgrind Fintech | 2021–2022
- Helped migrate the onboarding backend incrementally from Express to NestJS, route by route, behind the same API gateway.
- Gave a meetup talk about the migration in 2022.
- Technologies: Node.js, Express, NestJS, TypeORM, Prisma.

BankID Identity Verification Flow | Älvgrind Fintech | 2022
- Built a new onboarding identity step using Swedish BankID, including QR-code and same-device flows through a provider SDK.
- A/B tested on 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Technologies: React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS ECS.

Secure Document Upload | Älvgrind Fintech | 2023
- Built an ID-document upload flow supporting files up to 20 MB, with S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV virus scanning in Lambda, and scan-status updates through SQS into PostgreSQL.
- Technologies: AWS S3, Lambda, SQS, NestJS, PostgreSQL.

Ferry Ticket Mobile App | Sjöbris Digital, for a ferry operator | 2019–2020
- Led the technical delivery and built most of a React Native app for buying and showing ferry tickets offline. The app reached approximately 50,000 downloads.
- Technologies: React Native, TypeScript, Node.js, Firebase Cloud Messaging.

PERSONAL PROJECTS

Home Assistant Integrations | 2022–Present
- Built two small custom home-automation integrations, published on GitHub with approximately 40 stars combined.
- Technologies: Python (basic), YAML

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear seniority, relevant technical breadth, and several quantified outcomes. The BankID conversion increase and ferry-app download figure provide credible impact, while the secure document workflow demonstrates practical security awareness. The acting team-lead wording is appropriately accurate and does not overstate the temporary responsibility. The main content weakness is some repetition between Professional Experience and Selected Projects, plus limited evidence for testing, accessibility, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, Git workflows, and English proficiency. Contact details are still placeholders, so the document is not application-ready until those are replaced.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The single-column section structure, standard headings, plain text bullets, conventional dates, and explicit technology names should parse well in ATS systems. Keyword coverage is strong for React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, AWS, GraphQL, React Native, and A/B testing. AI screening probability is high for the core full-stack requirement. Screening may be weaker for accessibility, automated testing, Git, OWASP/authentication, privacy, Docker, Next.js, Storybook, and healthcare terminology because these are not supported by the supplied candidate information and therefore should not be added. Replace bracketed contact placeholders before submission and ensure the actual LinkedIn, GitHub, or portfolio URLs are written as readable URLs.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the core role: the CV demonstrates substantially more than the required React/TypeScript experience, Node.js backend work, SQL/PostgreSQL, NestJS, AWS, security-related workflows, and analytics/A/B testing. The BankID and document-upload work is especially relevant to Verdane Care's privacy-by-default and regulated-data context, although it is fintech rather than healthcare. The temporary team-lead experience supports collaboration and mentoring potential. The supplied material does not establish automated testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, OWASP knowledge, health-data privacy, Next.js/SSR, Docker, Storybook/design systems, German/Croatian, or explicit fluent English; these are gaps or unsupported requirements rather than CV-writing defects. The CV should not claim them.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / APPLICATION READINESS
1. In the header, replace every placeholder—"[SURNAME]", "[EMAIL]", "[PHONE]", "[LINKEDIN]", and "[GITHUB / PORTFOLIO]"—with the candidate's real details and complete URLs. Keep the links in plain text so ATS software can parse them.

2. In the Professional Experience section, reduce duplication with Selected Projects. Keep the detailed project entries for BankID, Secure Document Upload, and the ferry app, but shorten the corresponding experience bullets to role-level responsibilities and outcomes. For example, under Älvgrind Fintech, retain the conversion result and leadership bullet, then replace the repeated implementation bullets with a concise scope statement such as: "Develop onboarding features and maintain the onboarding BFF using React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, GraphQL, and AWS." This will make the CV more concise without removing evidence.

3. In the Professional Summary, replace "Experienced in onboarding and identity-verification features, secure document workflows, and leading delivery on a customer-facing mobile app" with wording that more directly reflects the target role while remaining truthful: "Experienced in patient-adjacent, customer-facing product development, identity verification, secure document workflows, and end-to-end delivery of web and mobile features." Do not call the experience healthcare or patient-facing unless that is factually accurate; the current fintech and ferry-app wording is the evidence available.

MINOR ENHANCEMENTS
4. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Databases and data" to "Databases / ORM" and format the entries consistently, for example: "PostgreSQL; TypeORM; Prisma." This improves keyword parsing and reduces ambiguity about what the candidate has used directly.

5. In the acting-team-lead bullet under Älvgrind Fintech, make the temporary nature and activities even clearer by changing it to: "Acted as team lead for four months in 2024 during the team lead's parental leave, conducting 1:1s and sprint planning." This preserves the accurate non-official status while foregrounding leadership and collaboration keywords.

6. In the ferry-app entry, change "Led the technical delivery and built most of a React Native app" to "Served as tech lead in a two-developer team, led technical delivery, and built most of a React Native app." This aligns more closely with the candidate's original information and makes the team context explicit.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured, professional CV with strong evidence of seniority, relevant technologies, ownership, and measurable outcomes. The BankID conversion result, secure document-upload implementation, incremental Express-to-NestJS migration, and 50,000-download mobile app are especially persuasive. The distinction between frontend strength, backend experience, and limited Terraform/Python depth is appropriately credible. Main content weaknesses are incomplete evidence for several explicit requirements, some repetition between Professional Experience and Selected Projects, and the absence of contact details, languages, Git/testing evidence, accessibility evidence, and a more targeted connection to patient-facing product development. The four-month acting-team-lead experience is accurately described and should not be presented as a permanent leadership title.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses conventional section headings, plain text, standard date formats, searchable technology names, and no tables, columns, icons, graphics, or unusual formatting. React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, AWS, GraphQL, A/B testing, and security-related implementation terms should parse well. AI screening probability is medium-high for the core React/TypeScript/Node.js/PostgreSQL match, but lower for the complete role because the document does not show automated testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web accessibility, English, or Docker. The duplicated project content may dilute keyword relevance slightly, although it does not create a parsing problem.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a strong match for the core full-stack stack: it demonstrates substantially more than the required two years of React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend work, SQL/PostgreSQL, NestJS, AWS, measurable A/B testing, and security-conscious workflows. The fintech onboarding and identity/document-verification work provides relevant evidence for privacy-sensitive and regulated software, although it is not healthcare experience. The ferry application demonstrates user-facing mobile-product ownership and offline usability. The document does not establish semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility basics, automated unit/integration/end-to-end testing, Git workflows, Next.js/server-side rendering, Docker, design systems, Storybook, German, or Croatian. English is supported by the original candidate material but is not shown in the CV. The strongest company-value alignment is with privacy-conscious implementation, reducing user friction, and customer-facing product impact; explicit healthcare, WCAG 2.2 AA, and clinic-user experience are not supported by the candidate material.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None detected. The CV's claims are supported by the Original Candidate Information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. At the top of the CV, directly below the name and headline, add the candidate's real phone number, email address, LinkedIn/GitHub URL if applicable, and current professional location if the candidate wants those details included. Do not invent or infer any contact information.
2. In the Professional Summary, retain the current seniority and technology claims but make the role match more explicit by changing the opening to: "Senior full-stack/frontend engineer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications, including 2+ years building React and TypeScript features backed by Node.js and PostgreSQL." This uses the job's terminology without adding unsupported experience.
3. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Databases and data" to "Databases and SQL" and list "PostgreSQL" first. This improves matching for the job's explicit SQL requirement without claiming experience with an unlisted database.
4. In the Technical Skills section, add a short "Security and delivery" category containing only supported terms such as "BankID identity verification, secure document upload, S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV virus scanning, AWS Lambda, SQS, and A/B testing." Do not add OWASP, authentication, GDPR, WCAG, Docker, Jest, Playwright, Git, or other technologies not supported by the Original Candidate Information.
5. Near the end of the CV, add a "Languages" section with "English — fluent" based on the English-language original candidate material. Do not add German or Croatian.
6. Reduce repetition between Professional Experience and Selected Projects. Keep the detailed measurable project bullets in Selected Projects, and shorten the corresponding experience bullets to emphasize role scope and ownership. For example, under Älvgrind Fintech, retain the technology and responsibility summary, then use "Selected projects below include measurable outcomes for identity verification and secure document handling" rather than repeating the full implementation details.
7. In the Professional Experience section under Älvgrind Fintech, clarify the leadership scope without overstating the title by changing "Served as acting team lead for four months in 2024 during the team lead’s parental leave, including 1:1s and sprint planning" to "Acting team lead for four months in 2024 during the team lead’s parental leave; conducted 1:1s and facilitated sprint planning." 
8. In the Professional Experience section under Nordkust Media, add any truthful scope already known to the candidate, such as the technologies used or the type of newspaper-web work, only if those details are documented elsewhere by the candidate. Otherwise, leave the entry concise rather than inventing detail.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible, well-structured CV with clear progression from Developer to Full-Stack Developer and acting team-lead experience. The strongest content is the selected-project section: it provides concrete technologies, responsibilities, and measurable outcomes such as the increase in onboarding conversion from 61% to 74% and approximately 50,000 mobile-app downloads. The summary is appropriately honest about frontend strength while still demonstrating relevant backend experience. The main content weaknesses are the absence of contact details or profile links, limited evidence of several standard engineering practices, and a few slightly repetitive or generic skill entries. The document does not contain an apparent hallucination when compared with the original candidate information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly plain text, standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, and searchable keywords including React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, AWS, GraphQL, S3, Lambda, SQS, and A/B testing. It should parse well and has a moderate-to-high AI screening probability for the core TypeScript/React/Node.js role. Screening probability will be reduced for this specific vacancy because the CV does not contain evidence or keywords for automated testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, OWASP, or health-data privacy. These are candidate-evidence gaps rather than defects that can be solved by adding unsupported claims. Adding real contact, LinkedIn, and GitHub URLs would improve recruiter usability and provide more machine-readable profile information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with the central technical stack: it shows more than two years of professional React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend work, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, secure document handling, identity verification, and A/B testing. The BankID and secure-upload projects are particularly relevant to Verdane Care's emphasis on privacy, responsible handling of sensitive information, and frictionless patient-facing journeys. The acting team-lead experience also supports collaboration and sprint-planning expectations. The candidate material does not show professional healthcare or wellness experience, Next.js/server-side rendering, Docker, design systems or Storybook, German or Croatian, automated unit/end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, or explicit semantic HTML, responsive-layout, accessibility, OWASP, or health-data privacy experience. These are gaps in the candidate evidence, not CV rewriting defects. AWS familiarity and A/B testing are clearly aligned nice-to-have qualifications.
critique.improvement_instructions:

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. At the top of the CV, directly beneath “OSKAR,” add the candidate’s actual email address, telephone number, professional profile URL, and GitHub or portfolio URL if available. Do not add placeholder or invented details. This is important because the current CV gives the recruiter no direct contact or profile link.
2. In the Personal Projects section, turn “published on GitHub” into a clickable or plain-text GitHub URL if one exists. This makes the stated project evidence verifiable without adding any new claim.
3. In the Fullstack Developer role under Älvgrind Fintech AB, remove the generic bullet “Selected projects below include measurable outcomes for identity verification and secure document handling.” The projects section already provides those details; replacing this bullet with a concrete day-to-day contribution or deleting it will make the experience section tighter and less repetitive.
4. In the Technical Skills section, remove the duplicate “AWS Lambda” entry from “Security and delivery,” since Lambda is already listed under “Cloud and messaging.” Keep the more specific security evidence—“BankID identity verification,” “secure document upload,” “S3 presigned URLs,” and “ClamAV virus scanning”—because those are supported by the project history.
5. In the Technical Skills section, consider changing “Other” to “Additional technologies” and retain the qualification levels exactly as supported: “Terraform (small edits)” and “Python (basic).” This makes the scope of those skills clearer and avoids presenting limited exposure as senior-level expertise.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible technical CV with a clear structure, relevant project evidence, and useful quantified outcomes, especially the 61% to 74% onboarding conversion increase and approximately 50,000 app downloads. The experience is presented concisely and the acting team-lead status is accurately qualified. The main content weaknesses are the absence of contact details and a languages section, limited detail in the Nordkust Media role, and some duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects. The opening phrase "Senior full-stack/frontend engineer" is slightly awkward and could be made more precise. Overall, the document is professional and persuasive for the core React/TypeScript/Node.js profile, but it does not establish several must-have requirements from the advertisement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard section headings, readable text, conventional dates, and a straightforward skills taxonomy. Core terms such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, SQL-adjacent ORM technologies, AWS, GraphQL, and A/B testing are present and supported by the candidate material. AI screening probability is moderate to high for the core full-stack stack, but lower for this specific vacancy because the CV does not mention automated testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web accessibility, or explicit English-language proficiency. Do not add those keywords unless the candidate can substantiate them. The lack of contact information or a direct GitHub link also reduces recruiter usability, although it should not affect technical parsing.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the central engineering scope: it shows more than 2 years of professional React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend work, PostgreSQL, NestJS, AWS, customer-facing applications, sprint planning, and A/B testing. The identity-verification and secure-document projects are particularly relevant to Verdane Care's privacy-focused environment and demonstrate practical security-minded engineering. The fintech context is adjacent to the advertised regulated-environment preference, but the CV does not show healthcare, health-data privacy, GDPR, audit-request handling, WCAG 2.2 AA, accessibility, automated testing, Git workflows, Next.js, Docker, Storybook, or clinic-system integrations. The CV also does not establish German or Croatian. These are candidate-evidence gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting. The document does not currently communicate the company's user-centred themes as explicitly as it could, although the ferry app, onboarding work, and conversion result provide relevant evidence of customer-facing product work.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CV CHANGES
1. In the document header, add the candidate's actual phone number, email address, professional location, LinkedIn URL, and GitHub URL. Do not invent or generalize these details. This is important for recruiter usability and ATS profile matching.
2. In the Professional Summary, replace "Senior full-stack/frontend engineer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications, including 2+ years building React and TypeScript features backed by Node.js and PostgreSQL" with a more direct, ad-aligned version such as: "Senior frontend-focused full-stack engineer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications, including 2+ years of professional React and TypeScript development, Node.js backend services, and PostgreSQL/SQL database work." This preserves the candidate's stated frontend strength while using the job description's terminology.
3. In the Professional Summary, replace "Experienced in onboarding and identity-verification features, secure document workflows, and leading delivery on a customer-facing mobile app" with "Experienced in customer-facing onboarding and identity-verification features, secure document-upload workflows, and technical delivery of a customer-facing mobile app." This is more specific and connects the experience to patient-facing product development without claiming healthcare experience.
4. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Databases and SQL" to "Databases and SQL" only if the candidate is comfortable explicitly describing PostgreSQL work as SQL database work; otherwise retain the current heading. Under it, list "SQL, PostgreSQL, TypeORM, Prisma" so the exact SQL keyword is visible to ATS systems. Do not add database technologies not present in the source material.
5. In the Technical Skills section, rename "Security and delivery" to "Security and product delivery" and retain only the supported evidence: "BankID identity verification, secure document upload, S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV virus scanning, A/B testing." This makes the security relevance more searchable without incorrectly claiming OWASP expertise.
6. In the Fullstack Developer role at Älvgrind Fintech AB, revise the first bullet to: "Build customer-facing onboarding features with React and TypeScript, backed by Node.js/NestJS services, PostgreSQL, and AWS." This makes the frontend, backend, SQL, and cloud relationship explicit and uses the job advertisement's terminology.
7. In the Fullstack Developer role, revise the acting-lead bullet to: "Served as acting team lead for four months in 2024 during parental leave; conducted 1:1s and facilitated sprint planning." This is shorter and keeps the important qualification that the role was acting rather than an official permanent title.
8. In the Personal Projects section, add the actual GitHub repository URL for the Home Assistant integrations. The source material confirms that these projects are published on GitHub, so this is a supported way to demonstrate GitHub-based work without claiming a Git workflow in professional employment.
9. In the Developer role at Nordkust Media, add one or two concise bullets only if the candidate can substantiate the work, such as the types of web technologies used or the nature of the newspaper-site features. Do not add technologies or responsibilities that are not in the original candidate information; the current one-line entry is the least informative part of the experience section.
10. Add a "Languages" section near Technical Skills only with language levels the candidate can substantiate. The current CV does not document English proficiency, and the job requires fluent English; do not label English "fluent" solely because the application material is written in English.
